Hello

I have a hammer miner and wanted to know about the warranty. I am within
the 12 month period and noticed the screen is having issues. How do I go
about a replacement? I have attached a picture of the miner and my original
order is Shop····.

Please advise.
Handed to the team · Part needed (screen); JD to confirm and team to decide on sending it. Asked cust

Hello,

Thanks for the photos and the order number. They made this much easier to check.

I looked at both pictures. The miner itself looks healthy. The board lights are on, the power jack is seated, and the fan and heatsink look fine. The problem is only the small display on top. It shows coloured horizontal bands and a faint ghost image where your normal mining stats should be. That points to the display module, not the miner's hashing board. A screen fault like this usually doesn't stop the miner from working.

Please do one quick check so we can confirm it's only the screen. Unplug the miner for about 30 seconds and plug it back in. Then open the miner's web page in your browser (using its IP address from your router's device list) or check your pool's dashboard, and see whether it's still hashing. Reply to this email with what you find: whether the screen came back normal after the restart, and whether the hashrate looks right.

I've sent my findings and your photos to our technical team, noting that this looks like a display problem. Someone will pick up your ticket and email you with an answer, usually within one business day.

If you'd like a quicker chat in the meantime, our Discord community is very active at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf. Mention @nullhashrate, who is our hardware lead.

Best regards,
Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support

That is part of the problem.
I need to connect it to my new wifi and I am unable to connect to the miner
through wifi.
Is there a different way for me to connect to it?
Note to the team: I'll check how Hammer units recover Wi-Fi when the screen can't be read.
Searched the web · Hammer DC02 miner wifi setup access point 192.168.4.1
Note to the team: Checking our own Hammer setup guide for the Wi-Fi hotspot details.

Hello,

Thanks for explaining. Without a working screen you can't read the miner's IP or its setup prompt, so here are two ways to get it onto your new Wi-Fi without the display.

The first way is the most reliable. Bring back your old Wi-Fi network for a short while. If you still have the old router, plug it in. If you don't, set up a hotspot on your phone with exactly the same network name and password as your old Wi-Fi. Set the hotspot to 2.4 GHz, or turn on "maximize compatibility" on an iPhone. The miner should join it by itself within a few minutes. Your phone or old router will then list it as a connected device with its IP address. From a device on that same network, type that IP address into a browser to open the miner's dashboard. Go to the network settings, choose your new Wi-Fi, enter its password, then save and restart. The miner will move to your new network, and you'll find its new IP in your new router's list of connected devices.

The second way: after a restart, look at your phone's Wi-Fi list for a network created by the miner itself. That's the setup network it puts out on first boot. Our Hammer setup guide covers this step:
it walks through setup from unboxing to pool setup and the WiFi connection
. If that network appears, connect to it. The miner's setup page should open, where you can search for your new Wi-Fi, enter the password, save and restart. I can't promise the miner brings up that network when it can't find its saved Wi-Fi, so if you don't see it after a few minutes, use the first way.

Two tips that solve most of these cases. First, the miner only works with 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. Many new routers combine 2.4 and 5 GHz under one name, and that can stop it from joining. If yours has a setting to split the bands or turn on a 2.4 GHz network, that often fixes it. Second, the Wi-Fi on this unit is weak, so keep it close to the router while you set it up.

If neither way works, reply and tell me what you saw: whether the hotspot showed the miner as connected, and whether a miner network appeared in your phone's Wi-Fi list. You can also get help faster in our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf. Mention @nullhashrate, our hardware lead.

Best regards,
Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support
